data.narrative:
Magdrive is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Mark Stokes and Thomas Clayson that has raised $22.5M to date. The space sector comprises a fragmented competitor landscape: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) trading at a median 27.4x price-to-sales, and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs at varying stages.

Valuation triangulation is constrained by limited data availability. The stage-progression method is the sole applicable approach, applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage against the $22.5M raised proxy, yielding $56M. Peer-median analysis cannot be applied: while 14 same-sector private peers exist, zero qualify as same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient valuation alignment. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable because Magdrive's revenue is not disclosed—a near-universal constraint for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $65M, centered on $56M. This range reflects ±15% confidence bounds around the single applicable method. Primary uncertainties stem from the absence of narrowly-comparable seed-stage peers and undisclosed revenue, which precludes multiples-based cross-checks common in later-stage valuations. Any refinement would require additional transaction data or revenue disclosure.
